summary: A Network Host Status report covering May 8 to May 19, 1972. Testing was skipped on May 15 because of the attempt to install the new IMP system. The MIT-AI and Stanford PDP-10 hosts each became network servers. It was replaced by RFC 353.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 344 records ARPANET host roles and test results for May 8 through May 19, 1972. It notes that the MIT AI and Stanford PDP-10s became servers and that testing was skipped on May 15 during an IMP system installation attempt.

subtitle: A report of ARPANET host status from May 8 to May 19, 1972.

tldr.problem: Network participants needed current information about which ARPANET hosts were accessible and available as servers.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists host roles and daily test results from May 8 through May 19, with no testing on May 15 during an attempted IMP system installation.
tldr.outcome: RFC 344 updates RFC 342 and was later obsoleted by RFC 353; it reports that the MIT AI and Stanford PDP-10s became servers.

facts.value: MIT AI PDP-10 and Stanford PDP-10

sections.title: Reporting Period and New Servers
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from May 8 to May 19. During this period, the PDP-10 at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Group, Network Address 134, and the Stanford PDP-10, Network Address 11, each became Network servers.

No testing was done on May 15 because of an attempt to install the new IMP system. The report also lists hosts excluded from daily testing because they were users only or were not expected to operate regularly as servers.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIT AI and Stanford PDP-10s became network servers during this reporting period. Testing stopped for one day while an IMP system installation was attempted.

sections.title: Host Status and Test Results
sections.content:
The RFC includes one table of reported host roles or predictions and another table of daily connection tests. Test results use codes such as O for Open, D for Dead, H for Half Open, R for Refused, T for Timed out, and F for Full.

Full means the host opened a connection, said all Network ports were in use, and immediately closed the connection. Timed out means the host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables separate reported server roles from actual connection test results. F means all network ports were in use, and T means the connection did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: Hosts Not Included in Daily Tests
sections.content:
Hosts excluded from the daily table include Terminal IMPs intended as users and the Network Control Center computer, which was used solely to gather network statistics. The report also lists the PDP-10 at Case as not expected to function regularly as a server for at least two weeks.

Some table entries have a marker indicating that a site had warned it might not be available at those times. The RFC presents these notes alongside the test results.
sections.plainLanguage: Not every listed host was tested each day. The report explains which systems were user-only or expected to be unavailable, and marks announced periods of unavailability.
